status: post_readback_taxonomic-generality test fixed before species-specific endpoints
question: Is the species-specific exact-site chorus template shared across many frog taxa, or driven by a small subset?
population: Exactly the prior-only, physically stable focal-cell population used by NAAMP_SPECIES_SPECIFIC_SITE_TEMPLATE_V0_1.
species_model: Within each species, retain pair x species groups with both own_prior_strong=1 and 0. Demean wet_strong, own_prior_strong, generic_other_strong_rate and their rain interactions within pair x species; fit the same no-intercept route-clustered model used in the pooled template analysis.
species_estimability: A species is estimable with >=20 informative pair x species groups and >=10 routes.
summaries: Number and fraction of estimable species with positive own-memory coefficient.
Number and fraction with complete 95% CI >0.
One-sided exact sign test against 50% positive.
Median and interquartile range of species-specific own-memory coefficients.
Pooled leave-one-species-out own-memory coefficient for every species.
primary_rule: Broad taxonomic template generality is supported if >=15 species are estimable, the one-sided sign test is P<0.05, and every leave-one-species-out pooled own-memory coefficient remains >0.
sensitivity: Repeat the sign summary in same-observer pairs when >=12 species are estimable.
interpretation: Support means the exact-site template is distributed across taxa in the NAAMP species pool, not that every species shows a significant effect.
Species-specific precision differs with occurrence frequency.
This does not establish cross-continental universality or a shared physiological mechanism.
